candidates.name: ropensci/skynet
candidates.what_it_holds: Peer-reviewed rOpenSci R package with import_db1b() and import_t100() functions that parse raw BTS DB1B (Coupon/Ticket) and T-100 segment CSVs downloaded from transtats.bts.gov into tidy data frames, plus make_net_dir() to build directed air-transport networks (city-pair traffic, fares) with statistical edge filtering. Includes a convert_raw() helper to compress raw files to needed variables. Topics tagged: bts, transtats, rita, t100, db1b, bureau-of-transport-statistics. Does not fetch On-Time Performance data. No raw data committed (BYO download from BTS website); this is a tidying/network-construction method, not a stored dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #10 (airline capacity/traffic as a travel-demand kernel analogue for ABNB nights) — a maintained, peer-reviewed method for turning raw BTS T-100 (city-pair capacity/seats/departures) and DB1B (fare/itinerary) files into usable panels, saving the team from writing a T-100/DB1B parser from scratch.
candidates.geography: US domestic + international segments touching the US (BTS scope)
candidates.time_coverage: Whatever vintage of T-100/DB1B the user downloads from BTS (historical archive back to 1990s available at source)
candidates.size_hint: Method only, no committed data; T-100/DB1B source files are large (DB1B ~GB-scale per quarter)
candidates.license: rOpenSci package, GPL-family typical (license file present, not read in full)
candidates.last_activity: Last updated 2024-09-12 per GitHub topic page

candidates.name: VijayChamakuri/hub-delay-audit
candidates.what_it_holds: Auditing minimum-connection-time standards at 15 major US hub airports (SFO, EWR, LGA, ORD, BOS, JFK, LAX, MSP, SLC, SEA, PHX, CLT, DEN, DFW, ATL) using BTS On-Time Performance (Jan 2019, ~584k rows) and DB1B Coupon Survey (Q1 2019, ~9.8M rows) data; analysis.py computes carrier-hub pair statistics across 69 carrier-hub pairs / 5 major carriers (AA, DL, UA, WN, AS), ~91.5% of sample volume. Raw data not committed (download instructions only); single-commit repo.
candidates.why_useful: A working, documented example of pulling and joining BTS On-Time Performance with DB1B at hub-airport granularity — reusable as a template even though the specific window (Jan-Mar 2019) is stale and would need re-pointing at current quarters for a live air-travel-demand proxy.
candidates.size_hint: ~584k rows OTP + ~9.8M rows DB1B (not committed, download only)

candidates.name: simonpcouch/anyflights
candidates.what_it_holds: CRAN-published R package (317 commits) generalizing nycflights13 to any FAA airport/year: get_flights(), get_weather(), get_airports(), get_airlines(), get_planes() pull flight-level departure records (built on underlying FAA/BTS on-time data feeds), hourly weather, and airport/airline/aircraft metadata for a user-specified station+year+month; can bundle results into a data-only R package. Notes FAA usually posts full-year data in Feb/March of the following year (i.e., a lag to be aware of for nowcasting).
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose, maintained client for pulling flight-level US air-travel data (a step toward T-100/OTP-style capacity and delay series) by any airport and year, which could be pointed at major leisure gateway airports (MCO, LAS, HNL, MIA) as a demand-kernel proxy alongside TSA throughput; also documents the FAA data-release lag relevant to point-in-time discipline.
candidates.time_coverage: Any year/month FAA has published (with ~1 year publication lag noted)
candidates.size_hint: Method only; flight-level, so volume scales with airport size
candidates.license: CRAN package, MIT-typical (not confirmed in fetch)

candidates.name: john-otienoh/Aviation_OTP_Pipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: Containerized Airflow + PostgreSQL pipeline computing industry-standard aviation on-time-performance reliability metrics from BTS On-Time Performance CSVs; ships only a 100-row synthetic prototype file (bts_ontime_simulated.csv, Jan2022-Dec2024 range simulated) — real BTS data is user-downloaded and gitignored above 100MB. MIT licensed, early-stage (3 commits).
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made ETL scaffold (Airflow DAG + Postgres schema) for ingesting monthly BTS OTP files on a recurring basis, which could shortcut building a repeatable pull for a live delay/capacity monitor; data itself is not included so value is purely as tooling.
candidates.time_coverage: Pipeline designed for any month; prototype simulates Jan2022-Dec2024
candidates.size_hint: Prototype ships 100 rows only; real data external

candidates.name: lienas/us-flight-delays-eda
candidates.what_it_holds: EDA notebooks over a ~2 million-row / ~644k-flight sample of BTS On-Time domestic flight data spanning 2010-2019 (22 reporting carriers); raw airline_2m.csv (~880MB) not committed (exceeds GitHub's 100MB limit) — README points to the official BTS On-Time archive for the download. No 2020+ data (COVID-affected 2020 explicitly excluded).
candidates.why_useful: A worked decade-long (2010-2019) carrier-level delay panel definition that could be re-pulled and extended through 2026 from the same BTS On-Time archive if a longer historical baseline for airline capacity/reliability is needed; itself contributes no new data since the file isn't committed and stops in 2019.

candidates.name: Gaurav0502/us-domestic-flights
candidates.what_it_holds: Quarto EDAV project analyzing punctuality/delay patterns for 2023 flights to/from NYC-area airports (JFK, LGA, EWR), built on the R anyflights() package (which itself wraps FAA/BTS on-time feeds); data/README.md gives download instructions rather than committing raw files; 50 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A narrow, NYC-specific 2023 flight punctuality slice — could be a cross-check for NYC-market travel-demand timing (NYC is one of the team's 13-city Inside Airbnb panel cities) but is single-year and not a stored dataset.
candidates.size_hint: not specified; generated via anyflights, not committed

candidates.name: mylee04/airport-now
candidates.what_it_holds: Live TypeScript/React/Vercel dashboard ('airport-now') aggregating real-time TSA checkpoint wait times (30 US airports, via official airport APIs/public pages), flight boards, nearby air-traffic, and crowdsourced traveler wait reports. Explicitly stores NO historical data: community reports live only in temporary Vercel runtime storage and auto-expire after 2 hours; no database, no committed dataset. Last review of its wait-source survey dated 2026-03-17. No license file found.
candidates.why_useful: Shows there is a live TSA-wait-time aggregation source covering 30 airports that could in principle be polled going forward to build a point-in-time throughput/congestion series, but as shipped it persists nothing — any use requires standing up your own scraper against the same 30 airport APIs it lists (a TOS question, not to be run per repo rules) or reading its source for the list of underlying airport APIs it hits.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: TSA throughput (daily, already held per CONTEXT.md item list) — this is finer-grained (per-checkpoint, real-time) but retains no history, so does not extend the held series

candidates.name: vega/vega-datasets
candidates.what_it_holds: Widely-used vega/vega-lite example-data hub (70+ datasets) including committed flight files derived from historical BTS on-time data: flights-airport.csv (airport-pair aggregated counts), flights-3m.parquet (3 million flight records), flights-200k.arrow/json, flights-20k/10k/5k/2k.json, and airports.csv (airport metadata/coordinates). These are the well-known anonymized/sampled flight-delay teaching datasets (originating ~2001-2016 vintage per common knowledge of this dataset family) rather than a live or recent BTS pull.
candidates.why_useful: A genuinely large, already-tidied, committed (not download-only) US flight-count/delay dataset with an airport-pair aggregation file — useful only as a structural template (schema, airport-pair aggregation pattern) since the vintage is old and not point-in-time; low direct value for a 2026 pitch.
candidates.time_coverage: Legacy vintage (dataset family originates from a fixed historical year, not refreshed)
candidates.last_activity: actively maintained repo (general vega ecosystem), but flight files are static/legacy
